Package frc.robot.subsystems.elevator

Class ElevatorSubsystem

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.elevator.AbstractElevatorSubsystem
frc.robot.subsystems.elevator.ElevatorSubsystem
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem, Subsystem, AutoCloseable
public class ElevatorSubsystem extends AbstractElevatorSubsystem
The elevator implementation robot teams instantiate against real hardware.

This class talks to motors directly. There is no IO layer between it and the mechanism: the position loop, the encoder scaling, and the motor commands all live here, which is where a team integrating this library will actually be working. Simulation is a separate class — SimElevatorSubsystem — rather than a second IO behind the same subsystem, so a team reading this file sees only the code that runs on their robot.

What this class does

  • Drives a leader/follower motor pair through WPILib's MotorController abstraction, so it works with any PWMSparkMax, PWMTalonFX, PWMSparkFlex, or PWMVictorSPX without change. Commands go to both controllers directly rather than through WPILib's MotorControllerGroup, which is deprecated for removal; a vendor implementation would instead make the follower mirror the leader in the controller's own firmware. A team with a vendor library should subclass this and override applyVolts(double) to use the vendor's API, which gives onboard control and better telemetry.
  • Closes the position loop with a WPILib PIDController plus ElevatorFeedforward.
  • Reads travel from a quadrature Encoder and conditionally from limit switches.

Hardware IDs come from the caller. Everything wired — CAN IDs, encoder channels, limit switch channels, inversion — is a constructor argument, so a team configures their robot without editing library source. 


 ElevatorSubsystem elevator = new ElevatorSubsystem(
     new PWMSparkMax(2),                    // leader
     new PWMSparkMax(3),                    // follower
     true,                                  // follower inverted
     new Encoder(0, 1),                     // quadrature encoder
     new DigitalInput(4),                   // lower limit
     new DigitalInput(5),                   // upper limit
     ElevatorHardware.CONSTANTS);           // mechanism description

Gains are a starting point. They come from Constants.HardwareDefaults and are sized so a plausible mechanism moves under control on first run. Every team must tune on their own hardware, because gains depend on gearing, mass, and friction this library cannot know. Call setGains(double, double, double) to retune at runtime.

  • Constructor Details

    • ElevatorSubsystem

      public ElevatorSubsystem(edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.motorcontrol.MotorController leader, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.motorcontrol.MotorController follower, boolean followerInverted, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.Encoder encoder, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.DigitalInput lowerLimit, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.DigitalInput upperLimit, ElevatorConstants constants)
      Creates an elevator over WPILib motor controllers and sensors.
      Parameters:
      leader - the motor controller that receives commands
      follower - the motor controller that mirrors the leader
      followerInverted - whether the follower turns opposite the leader
      encoder - a quadrature encoder measuring carriage travel
      lowerLimit - the lower travel limit switch, or null if the mechanism has none
      upperLimit - the upper travel limit switch, or null if the mechanism has none
      constants - the physical description of the mechanism

    • holdPosition

      protected void holdPosition(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Distance position)
      Description copied from class: AbstractElevatorSubsystem
      /** Drives the carriage to hold position.

      Called once per loop while the mechanism is enabled. Implementations close the loop however suits their hardware: a vendor motor controller's onboard position control, or a WPILib PIDController plus feedforward, as ElevatorSubsystem and SimElevatorSubsystem both do.

      position is already clamped to the travel range, so implementations need not re-validate it.

      Specified by:
      holdPosition in class AbstractElevatorSubsystem
      Parameters:
      position - the height to hold, measured from the zero position

    • driveOpenLoop

      protected void driveOpenLoop(double velocityMetersPerSecond)
      Description copied from class: AbstractElevatorSubsystem
      Drives the carriage open-loop at a velocity.

      Not reached from any command in this API; it exists so a subclass can build a homing routine — drive into the lower stop until AbstractElevatorSubsystem.isAtLowerLimit() trips, then AbstractElevatorSubsystem.zeroPosition() — without reaching around the abstraction for raw voltage.

      Specified by:
      driveOpenLoop in class AbstractElevatorSubsystem
      Parameters:
      velocityMetersPerSecond - the velocity to drive at, positive raising the carriage

    • releaseOutput

      protected void releaseOutput()
      Description copied from class: AbstractElevatorSubsystem
      Stops commanding the mechanism.

      Called while idle and on SubsystemBase.stop(). Whether the carriage then holds or sags is the hardware's brake mode, not a decision this method makes.

      Specified by:
      releaseOutput in class AbstractElevatorSubsystem
